subject: MediaLabs: Pilot SLO/Compromise & Pricing — Exec Approval Needed
messages:
From: Denise Park <denise.park@medialabs.io>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood pilot — initial ask on SLO/credits and discount

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We are excited to move forward with a 12-month pilot of Redwood Dedicated for inference in our US region. Two items that surfaced on our side from Procurement and our CTO:

- Uptime: they want a written uptime target of 99.5% (we understand you normally offer 99.9% for Dedicated).
- Service credit cap: they want the total monthly service credit capped at 5% of monthly spend for any given month.
- Latency: our internal SREs would like a p95 inference latency SLO of <= 180ms for the batch profile we shared.
- Commercial: They asked whether a 20% committed-use discount is possible if we sign a 12-month reserved capacity agreement and prepay 6 months.

Attaching our procurement intent and the usage profile (MediaLabs_SOW_intent.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate these nonstandard SLO/credit caps and the discount? If not, what alternatives do you recommend? We are trying to avoid a long legal round trip but need something that Procurement can sign off on quickly.

Thanks,
Denise Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
MediaLabs Inc.

-----

Ben / Marissa — forwarding MediaLabs' procurement ask. Key asks below (they want a short-form approval so Procurement can sign):

- Uptime target requested: 99.5% (we normally offer 99.9% for Dedicated).
- Service credit cap requested: 5% of monthly spend.
- Latency SLO (p95): <= 180ms for the provided batch profile.
- Commercial: 20% discount for 12-month reserved capacity if they prepay 6 months.

My read: pilot is high strategic value (large brand, reference potential). Economics hit depends on how we price the reserve. Ben, can you run a quick model for worst-case credits at 99.5% vs 99.9% and the impact of a 20% prepay? Jonas / Lauren, any redline/legal flags on capping credits at 5%?

Attached: ML_SLO_proposal_redline.docx and pilot_pricing_model.xlsx (draft).

I think this should be handled as a Deal Desk escalation — I'm proposing we seek one-time exec sign-off for the pilot with the below boundaries:
  1) Pilot term: 12 months, but commercial concession limited to initial 6 months of prepaid pricing.
  2) SLO amendment as a pilot schedule, auto-reverts to standard contract on renewal.
  3) Cap service credits at 5% for pilot months only.
  4) Add an operational SLA clause: if we observe >2 incidents in a rolling 30-day window, we reserve right to suspend pilot discount and require migration to standard terms.

If everyone is comfortable, I'll build a short memo for Marissa to sign off (Approve/Decline).

—Camila

Camila — quick numbers after the draft model: attached 'pilot_pricing_model.xlsx' has scenario tabs. TL;DR:

- If we accept 99.5% uptime vs our baseline 99.9%, expected monthly credits under a conservative outage model increase from ~0.8% to ~3.6% of monthly spend. With the proposed 5% cap, worst-case liability is bounded which makes the concession acceptable commercially for a pilot.
- 20% prepay discount for 12 months: if they truly prepay 6 months, our cashflow improves but we eat margin. Net ARR impact over 12 months is roughly -12% ARR at current unit economics (assuming no additional overages).
- My recommendation: Approve pilot on the requested SLO terms with conditions:
    * Service credit cap = 5% for pilot months only.
    * Pilot limited to a single region (us-west) and one logical cluster to limit blast radius.
    * Add a measurement clause: weekly latency reports and a remediation runbook; if p95 > 250ms for 3 consecutive weeks, we trigger a performance review and can pause discounts.
    * Approve the 20% prepay if they prepay at least 50% of the 12-month commitment (so 6 months minimum).

I'll draft a short commercial memo if you want to escalate to Marissa for exec sign-off.

—Ben
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

Ben / Camila — legal notes: a few items we must include if we cap credits and change uptime language:

1) The SLO amendment must be a named schedule to the master services agreement and explicitly state the cap applies only to monetary credits and not other remedies (e.g., termination rights) unless we explicitly waive them.
2) We need explicit audit and telemetry access during the pilot — add a 'reasonable access' clause so Redwood can validate incident windows.
3) Data residency/third-party access: ensure any monitoring or caching does not violate their data residency statement.
4) Sunset language: auto-revert to standard SLOs on renewal and require written acknowledgement at renewal time.

I'll prepare redline language; please confirm we want these in the pilot schedule.

—Jonas
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Subject: EXEC APPROVAL REQUEST — MediaLabs pilot SLO & commercial concessions

Marissa — asking for a single-exec decision to close MediaLabs this week. Below is the concise approval ask and the recommended guardrails: 

Approval ask (single decision):
  * Approve one-time pilot concession for MediaLabs:
    - Uptime target: 99.5% (pilot schedule)
    - Service credit cap: 5% of monthly spend (pilot months only)
    - Latency SLO: p95 <= 180ms; operational reporting requirements attached
    - Commercial: 20% committed-use discount for 12-month reserved capacity if MediaLabs prepays at least 6 months

Recommended guardrails (required if approved):
  1) Pilot confined to us-west region and single cluster.
  2) Pilot limited to 12 months but pricing concession limited to first 6 months; auto-revert at renewal.
  3) If >2 incidents in a rolling 30-day window OR p95 > 250ms for 3 consecutive weeks, pause discounts and trigger remediation.
  4) Legal to include audit access and explicit sunset language in the pilot schedule.
  5) Service credit cap applies to monetary credits only; termination rights unaffected unless exec explicitly waives them.

Attachments: ML_SLO_proposal_redline.docx, pilot_pricing_model.xlsx, MediaLabs_SOW_intent.pdf. DocuSign envelope prepared: https://www.docusign.com/ML-2026-Pilot-Approval (link attached).

Decision options for Marissa:
  - APPROVE: grant the pilot concessions under the guardrails above; instruct me to send the schedule to MediaLabs and route to DocuSign.
  - DECLINE: keep standard SLOs and pricing; ask me to propose alternatives (e.g., 10% discount, no SLO change).

Requesting a reply by EOD today so we can keep momentum.

Thanks — I recommend APPROVE with the guardrails.

—Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
